title: Service resilience & cost governance strategy session

transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2026-07-14 16:00 PDT | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Alex Mercer, Priya Nair, Jordan Lee, Sam Ortiz (Redwood); Lena Roth, Arjun Patel, Mei Chen, Carlos Vega, Rita Singh (Horizon Retail Labs)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): cost spike in june, two short outages, request for dedicated pilot and security docs.

[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account.
[00:08] Lena Roth: Hi Alex, Lena here. Thanks.
[00:10] Arjun Patel: Arjun joining.
[00:12] Mei Chen: Mei here.
[00:14] Carlos Vega: Carlos for finance.
[00:15] Rita Singh: Rita from security.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Jordan from CS, hi all.
[00:20] Alex Mercer: Cool. Agenda — usage & billing anomaly, reliability recap, Dedicated pilot idea, security ask, next steps. Any additions?
[00:28] Lena Roth: No, that's good. We want to focus on the cost spike and make sure the reliability work is solid before Q4 commit.
[00:35] Priya Nair: I'll jump into the technicals on the incidents later — quick note, some transcription may show KV cash instead of KV cache, so apologies if that shows up in notes.
[00:45] Carlos Vega: To be clear, finance saw an unexpected 34% increase month-over-month in hosted inference costs for June. We need a line item level explanation.
[00:57] Alex Mercer: Understood. We dug preliminarily into routing and autoscale events; I'll share the raw breakdown. It looks like a combination of a late-night burst plus a model variant fallback that used a larger model for about two hours.
[01:10] Mei Chen: That fallback — is that the automatic degrade to the higher-capacity replica or the other way around?
[01:14] Priya Nair: The transcript from our infra shows a fallback to the safer variant due to transient memory pressure. It ironically used a bigger model (we label B-v2) because of compatibility — the runtime picked a compatible variant that had different perf/cost.
[01:28] Arjun Patel: Can you show traces where the KV cache misses spike? Our cache hit rate dropping would explain per-token cost.
[01:34] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll attach the trace. I saw a window around 02:10 UTC where prefix caching warmed slowly after a deploy, so more tokens went to full forward passes.
[01:46] Lena Roth: There were two small incidents last month that our oncall logged as P0 briefly — do you have root cause notes?
[01:53] Jordan Lee: I can summarize. Incident A (June 9) — a node OOM triggered fallback routing; Incident B (June 22) — a networking flake in our region caused a short capacity drop which triggered autoscale and slightly higher on-demand usage. Both were mitigated by our fallback policies and recovery hooks.
[02:12] Mei Chen: Were either related to quantization profiles? We recently pushed a quantized shard for lower-cost inference.
[02:18] Priya Nair: Good call — there was a mismatch with a quantization profile vs B-v2 which exacerbated memory usage. We're putting a guard in the onboarding pipeline so mismatched profiles won't be used in routable stacks.
[02:32] Carlos Vega: For finance, we just need the per-model, per-route cost. If the fallback used B-v2 for two hours, we need to see the delta.
[02:41] Alex Mercer: We'll produce that. We'll also show cost normalized by request type and token-length bucket, since median token length increased for a few new flows you rolled out.
[02:53] Rita Singh: From security, we need SOC2 artifact links, an audit trail for model changes, and confirmation of KMS usage for customer keys.
[03:03] Jordan Lee: We'll send our SOC2 summary and the audit checklist. We do use KMS — for Hosted we have envelope encryption; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS.
[03:16] Rita Singh: Can you confirm HSM options? It's mandated for PII flows.
[03:20] Sam Ortiz: Yes, we support HSM via our Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed keys depending on your compliance setup. We'll include options in the scoping doc.
[03:30] Lena Roth: The team's leaning towards a Dedicated pilot to cap costs and control latency. What's the typical timeline and cost for a pilot?
[03:40] Alex Mercer: Pilot timeline varries — scoping, then a 4–8 week pilot in most cases. We'll draft a sizing template; Sam can run through sample commit tiers and SLA tiers.
[03:50] Sam Ortiz: For a pilot we usually propose a 6 week window: 1 week scoping and infra prep, 4 weeks run + perf validation, 1 week wrap and knowledge transfer. Costs depend on reservation level — we have burst options to prevent capacity shortages while you validate.
[04:08] Mei Chen: We need to validate median 512-token latencies under our traffic shape, and also check tail latencies during autoscale events.
[04:16] Priya Nair: We'll run a benchmark with your traffic replay and include tail-percentiles (p95/p99) and token-rate variability. We'll share the raw traces so your SREs can cross-check.
[04:27] Arjun Patel: Also include cold-start behavior for large-context requests. We see some token spikes when histories exceed 2048.
[04:35] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll include sequence-length stratified traces.
[04:40] Carlos Vega: Back to costs: if we move to Dedicated, how quickly do we see cost normalization? We need an example math before exec sign-off.
[04:49] Sam Ortiz: For steady-state workloads, Dedicated with proper batching and prefix caching typically reduces per-token costs by 30–60% depending on model mix. We'll produce an example case that matches your July request shape.
[05:02] Lena Roth: Ok good. On product roadmap alignment: we want a feature to pin model versions per route and more visible rollout metrics. How are those surfaced today?
[05:12] Jordan Lee: In Console we have per-route model pins, and a rollout dashboard showing traffic split and error rate. We can expose a pin-by-default flag for your account so devs don't accidentally use non-pinned variants.
[05:26] Mei Chen: That would help. Also want alerting thresholds for per-route cost burn so product managers know when a new feature is expensive.
[05:35] Alex Mercer: We can set per-route cost alerts and integrate with your PagerDuty/Slack channels. We'll propose default thresholds and you can tune.
[05:44] Lena Roth: On governance, we also need a retention policy control — some logs we must keep, others we must truncate. Can Redwood support configurable retention per route?
[05:53] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention is configurable per route and per-account; however, some hosted logs are subject to our platform retention limits unless you're on Dedicated or Private where you control retention.
[06:07] Carlos Vega: One more question: June's spike — will we see this again if we move to Dedicated?
[06:13] Priya Nair: Dedicated removes multi-tenant fallback surprises and gives you predictable allocation, but you still need caching and correct quantization profiles. The immediate spike drivers (memory pressure + fallback) would be mitigated in Dedicated.
[06:26] Arjun Patel: Can we get a runbook for incident response with Redwood for the pilot? We want clear SLAs and escalation paths.
[06:33] Sam Ortiz: We'll include an escalation and runbook in the pilot docs — names, pager contacts, expected RTO/RPO for different tiers.
[06:41] Mei Chen: Also, let's schedule a deep-dive technical session focused on the cache warming and fallback logic. Priya, can you lead that?
[06:48] Priya Nair: Happy to — propose 90 min session, SE-led with traces and a small replay harness.
[06:55] Lena Roth: Great. For budget, I need a one-pager for my CFO describing the pilot cost and expected ROI by month. Carlos, can you own internal finance ask?
07:02 Carlos Vega: Yes, I'll handle it.
[07:05] Alex Mercer: To recap, action items — we'll send cost breakdown, SOC2 docs, run latency benchmark, prepare pilot sizing. Any additional asks before we close?
[07:15] Rita Singh: Please include proof of key destruction and retention for deleted model artifacts — that's a compliance ask.
[07:21] Jordan Lee: Noted, will include artifact lifecycle notes.
[07:27] Lena Roth: OK thanks everyone. Let's tentatively aim for the scoping workshop week of July 20.
[07:34] Alex Mercer: I'll send a calendar invite for a 60-minute scoping workshop. Thanks all.

Notes about transcript quality: multiple speaker overlaps at 04:40–04:50, some jargon mis-recognized (e.g., K-V cash, B-v2 labelled differently), numeric timestamps approximated.

End of transcript.
